verdicts.evidence: Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes.
verdicts.reason: The agent disclosed recording in the opening turn, within the first minute.

verdicts.evidence: Before we get into anything, can I get your full name and date of birth, please?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked for full name and date of birth before discussing any details or quote, and the customer provided both.

verdicts.evidence: So tell me a bit about your situation. What's got you looking at life insurance right now?
verdicts.reason: Before recommending, the agent asked why the customer wants cover, then asked about the mortgage, dependants and employment.

verdicts.evidence: Coverage goes anywhere from $50,000 up to $750,000, there's no medical exam, acceptance is based on a few health questions, you pick a 10- or 20-year term, premiums are fixed for the whole term, and there's no cash value, it's pure protection.
verdicts.reason: Everything stated about coverage range, no exam, terms, fixed premiums, no cash value and the 30-day free look with full refund matches the product facts. No incorrect claims about price or exclusions.

verdicts.evidence: That's completely fine, there's no rush at all. Take whatever time you need.
verdicts.reason: The agent accepted the customer's decision to wait and applied no false urgency.

verdicts.evidence: I don't want to decide this today. I want to sit with <PERSON>, and maybe our daughter, and go through it properly.
verdicts.reason: No sale was completed; the customer deferred the decision, so consent was not required.

verdicts.evidence: Sure. So the main points again: up to $750,000 in coverage, no exam, 10 or 20 years, fixed premium, no cash value, 30-day free look with a full refund.
verdicts.reason: The customer disclosed a stroke and memory and word-finding difficulties. The agent repeated the key points when asked, explained terms, stopped pushing the questions when the customer was overwhelmed, supported involving his wife and daughter, offered an email summary and a callback, and said anyone could pick the call up again.
Doesn't apply in the CA market.
